stance_basis: testimony arguing Airport Spur primarily benefits business/trucking, predictions invalid, and poses safety risks to children
summary: Edward Zervic, a private citizen, testified at the July 11, 1974 Environmental Public Hearing opposing the Airport Spur. He argued that most airport-goers would use other routes, that the spur primarily benefits industry and trucking rather than residents, that 20-year traffic predictions are unreliable, and that errant trucks carrying hazardous chemicals near Hamlin-Garland School pose a danger to children. He also raised historical questions about why the spur was not built with I-94 and questioned the proportionality of air cargo versus passenger traffic growth.
complaint_summary: Zervic testified that most airport travelers would use other routes, that the Airport Spur primarily benefits industry and trucking, that 20-year traffic predictions are invalid, that errant trucks carrying hazardous chemicals near Hamlin-Garland School endanger children, and raised historical questions about why the spur was not built with I-94 and the intended use of College Avenue ramps.

Airport Spur will allow for more and faster movement of cargo and therefore, will benefit industry, business and trucking.
The movement of cargo, however, is not the primary benefit derived from the Airport Spur. It will also allow for safer and more efficient movement of passengers by both auto and rubber tired mass transit vehicles.
